name: PA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Reschenthaler with $4.2M raised and $990K on hand
Challenger Bradstock raised only ~$200K with minimal outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~3%
model.rationale: The R+17 district, a well-funded incumbent, and a heavily outspent challenger with no polling support all point to a safe Republican hold; markets agree at roughly 3% for the Democrat.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or unexpected incumbent scandal could tighten the race, but nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Guy Reschenthaler seeks another term in a southwestern Pennsylvania district that leans Republican by about 17 points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over $4.2 million and holding nearly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Alan Bradstock has raised about $200,000 with little outside help.

No public polls track the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 3% chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated and the fundamentals firmly favoring Republicans, the district remains a safe Republican seat.
